correctness.rationale: Stable 3-vertex cells have common within-cell outdegree one and are directed triangles; size-two stable cells are impossible. Between two triples the directed 3×3 cross-adjacency has constant row/column sum k, so k∈{0,3} is uniform and k∈{1,2} gives exactly a perfect matching or complement. Every automorphism preserves refinement cells and rotates each triangle by t_P∈Z/3; matching preservation imposes t_Q=sgn(π_PQ)t_P. Balanced signed components admit one free C3 rotation; a negative cycle gives t=−t, hence t=0 modulo 3. All compatible rotations preserve every arc; this proves full group and orbit partition, not just necessary conditions. Unbalanced signed cycle needs >=3 triple blocks => >=9 vertices. Independent reconstruction of explicit three-triangle witness verified degree partition 3,3,3/4,4,4/5,5,5 and unique automorphism among 27 possible classwise rotations; appending dominating singleton vertices maintains a negative cycle and rigid property. Inspected full verify.py with 2744 pattern families (2310 in-scope), but finite checks only corroborate the unbounded symbolic theorem.
residual_risks: Only tournaments with actual stable directed color-cell size<=3; no statement for larger blocks.

value.rationale: The theorem computes full automorphism groups and orbits from an elementary signed auxiliary graph rather than exhaustive permutations. It explains exact obstruction to refinability for unbounded tournament sizes with naturally small equitable color cells and gives a sharp threshold and rigid counterexample family; it is a structural classification, not just a finite computation.

final_claim: For any finite tournament with every actual stable directed one-dimensional color-refinement class of size <=3, Aut(T)≅(Z/3Z)^b, where b counts balanced connected components of a signed graph of minority matchings between 3-vertex cells; stable classes equal orbits iff all components balanced; the sharp first nonrefinable example has nine vertices and extends to every larger order.
